result:
The proposed answer of N is very likely wrong, and the "Final answer" line is also malformed, since it prints a function object (`<function N at 0x72e8929ed760>`) rather than a value.

The reasoning claims that each of the N solitons contributes exactly one pole and that there are no interaction poles. That is not justified. The solitons share the same mass and come from a single embedded eigenvalue of multiplicity N, so they are not independent. The determinant's polynomial structure should give more poles than N. I recall the source result as growing quadratically in N (something like N² or N(N+1)/2), not linearly, but I could not verify this. All of these candidates agree at N=1, so only N≥2 distinguishes them, and the answer N fails there.

VERDICT: REJECT
